title: Multi-Tenant SaaS Admin Dashboard

requirements.text: Organizations can self-onboard by creating a tenant (org name, subdomain/slug, first admin account)
Completing onboarding provisions an isolated tenant workspace and signs in the first admin
Each tenant has roles that grant sets of permissions, with default Admin and Member roles
Tenant admins can define custom roles by selecting from available permissions
Users are assigned one or more roles; effective permissions are the union of their roles' permissions
Permission-gated actions are enforced against the acting user's effective permissions
Admins invite users by email with assigned roles; invitees accept via link, set up account, and join the tenant
Admins can view pending invitations, resend, and revoke an invitation before acceptance
An immutable audit log records significant actions (who/what/when), viewable and filterable by actor, action type, and date range
A usage metrics dashboard shows per-tenant time-series metrics (active users, API volume, storage) over a selectable range
Admins can view the current plan, usage against plan limits, and upgrade or downgrade the plan
Tenants can configure SAML SSO via IdP metadata (entity ID, SSO URL, certificate); enabled tenants sign in via SAML
Admins can create named tenant-scoped API keys, list active keys (name, created, last-used), and revoke keys; secret shown only once at creation
Admins can toggle tenant-level feature flags from a list showing each flag's on/off state
Admins can request an asynchronous data export and are notified/download it when ready
Admins configure tenant-level settings (display name, subdomain/slug, default role for new members, default timezone)
Strict tenant data isolation is enforced so no tenant can access another tenant's data

hallucination_traps: Do not add reseller/partner hierarchies (explicitly out of scope)
Do not add per-seat/per-user billing (explicitly out of scope)
Do not add OIDC/OAuth SSO (only SAML is in scope; explicitly out of scope)
Do not invent a specific billing provider (e.g., Stripe) — none is named
Do not invent specific plan tiers or prices — none are stated
notes: A faithful parser should produce ~15-25 tasks and respect stated dependencies: nearly all tenant-scoped features depend on tenant onboarding; user invitations depend on RBAC (roles must exist); billing depends on usage metrics. It should treat tenant data isolation, RBAC enforcement, and audit-log recording as cross-cutting constraints applied across tasks rather than inventing provider/plan/pricing details.
